clue.text: Begs future replacement for this device

indicators.note: a replacement of these letters means putting them back in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone pleading for a new future is accused of using a trick to get it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' is the anagram signal: the ten letters of BEGS FUTURE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A subterfuge is a ruse or stratagem, a cunning trick used to get one's way.

clue.text: Uniform previously alluded to

explanation.surface: A dress code mentioned earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means unvarying, identical throughout; and 'the said' or aforementioned thing is referred to again with this word.

clue.text: Save new grain in this store

parts.note: save in the sense of except, as is bar ('all bar one')

explanation.surface: A farmer stores the fresh harvest in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb about keeping things, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm buildings for keeping harvested crops such as wheat are the classic example of this structure.

clue.text: Description of a study in which scholars have words!

definitions.text: Description of a study in which scholars have words!

parts.words: Description of a study in which scholars have words!
parts.note: 'have words' suggests a quarrel among academics, but the study really concerns words themselves: their origins and histories

explanation.surface: An account of academics squabbling in their research.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the study of word origins and the development of their meanings.

clue.text: Scale found where fish are dried

explanation.surface: Fish scales are found on the drying racks.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is less familiar: a flake is a frame or rack on which cod and other fish are laid out to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale is a thin chip or layer; separately, a rack or platform for drying fish carries the same name.

clue.text: Two fellows manufacturing headgear

parts.note: Glen is a man's name
Garry is a second man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of men are making hats.
explanation.walkthrough: A glengarry is a Scottish brimless cap with ribbons at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: This boat-shaped woollen cap is a traditional item of Highland dress, a kind of hat.

clue.text: Nearly a month's supply of brandy?

indicators.note: nearly a whole word means it loses its final letter here

parts.note: March is a month

explanation.surface: Enough brandy to last almost a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the last letter, H, from MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a spirit distilled from the skins and pips left after pressing grapes for wine.

clue.text: Mostly its action initially benefits one when ailing

definitions.text: Mostly its action initially benefits one when ailing

indicators.note: ailing means sick or out of sorts, so these letters are in a disordered state
mostly means all but the last letter of the word its is kept
initially points to the opening letter of benefits

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The drug's effect mainly helps a sick patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts IT from 'its'; 'initially' gives B; 'when ailing' shuffles IT + ACTION + B + I into the answer. The whole clue also describes the medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a medicine kills bacteria, so its effect generally helps a person who is ill with an infection.

clue.text: Reduced income journalists finally accepted

indicators.note: in tells us that the journalists' word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: the press is the collective term for journalists

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of accepted

explanation.surface: Journalists eventually agreed to a cut in pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed word 'income' must be split as 'in come': 'in' is the container signal and 'come' is the outer word, with PRESS put inside and D (the last of 'accepted') added.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezed into less space, made smaller.

clue.text: Pieeyed manufacturer having a good time

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing a person, standing for the noun

parts.note: pie-eyed is slang for drunk, as is merry
a maker is one who manufactures

explanation.surface: A drunken factory owner enjoying himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it describes the reveller rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveller is a person enjoying themselves at a party or festivity.

clue.text: Check the line of descent

explanation.surface: Verify a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To check means to halt the flow of something; a family's line of ancestry is also called a stock or this word.

clue.text: Efficient president supports firm labour leader

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: a firm is a business

indicators.note: leader takes the opening letter of labour

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A capable head of state backs a company's union boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts IKE under L in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being systematic and practical, as a well-run company is, means being efficient.

clue.text: Greedy person with a craving for bread

definitions.text: Greedy person with a craving for bread

parts.words: Greedy person with a craving for bread
parts.note: bread is slang for cash, and someone who grubs for it is grasping and avaricious

explanation.surface: A glutton who longs for loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A person obsessed with amassing cash by any means is greedy for 'bread' in its slang sense.

clue.text: Impartial priest and workman trapped by rising river

indicators.note: trapped by means the priest and workman are enclosed within the river
in a down clue rising means the river's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
Ven. (Venerable) is the title of an archdeacon
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A fair-minded cleric and a labourer are cut off by a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the river backwards, as it reads upward in a down entry; Ven. is the written title of an archdeacon (the Venerable), and 'hand' is a farm or factory worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating all sides equally and fairly is being impartial.

clue.text: Surprise warning given in examinees' translation

definitions.note: used as an adjective, as in a surprise attack

indicators.note: given in means the warning is placed inside the translation

parts.note: an unseen is a passage set in an exam for translation without preparation
fore is the warning shout in golf

explanation.surface: Students get an unexpected warning about their translation exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprise' works as an adjective here. FORE is the golfer's shout to warn people a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not predicted is unexpected, coming as a shock.

clue.text: Posh vehicle canopy seen around the island

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: around means the canopy word surrounds the letter for posh

parts.note: a canopy is a cover
U means upper class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A smart car with a hood is spotted touring the island.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British crossword convention. Vancouver Island lies off Canada's Pacific coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver Island is a large island in British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: Unofficial patrolman living at Gravesend, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: read as grave's end: the last letter of grave

explanation.surface: A self-appointed lawman lives in the Kent town of Gravesend.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravesend is a town in Kent; split as 'grave's end' it gives E. The surface town is the misdirection; 'possibly' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-appointed enforcer of law who acts without legal authority is an unofficial patrolman.

clue.text: Robust society clubs

parts.note: an iron constitution or will is robust

explanation.surface: A tough social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' are golf clubs with metal heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers use metal-headed sticks of this kind.

clue.text: Boy returns carrying award for girl

indicators.note: carrying means the boy's name holds the award inside
returns means the boy's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a boy's name
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A lad comes back with a prize for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses the boy's name to NAI; the OM (Order of Merit) is a British honour held by a small number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female name, from the Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Explosive ingredient Capone abandoned generically incorrect

indicators.note: incorrect means the remaining letters are wrongly ordered
abandoned means the gangster's name is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster has left, and the general description of an explosive's contents is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes AL out of GENERICALLY to leave GENERICLY, which 'incorrect' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Glycerine is nitrated to make nitroglycerine, the active component of dynamite.

clue.text: Tractability is the last word to a skilful Head

parts.note: amen is the final word of a prayer
able means skilful
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names like Shoeburyness

explanation.surface: Being docile is the final word for a capable headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a school head but is a headland; NESS is common in British place names for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easily managed and willing to comply is being docile, tractable.

clue.text: Series of books about a single composition

indicators.note: about means the books surround the other piece

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a series of books of the Bible
a single means one

explanation.surface: A book series is about a single piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: A nonet is a piece for nine performers.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a musical work written for nine instruments or voices.

clue.text: River identified in the Bronze Age

indicators.note: identified in means the answer can be spotted within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A river recognised as belonging to the Bronze Age.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'thE BROnze'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river in Spain.

clue.text: Furniture-maker has a drink with the King

parts.note: tea is a drink
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A cabinetmaker shares a cup with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furniture-maker' is not a carpenter but the hardwood furniture is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a durable tropical hardwood much used in cabinets and tables.

clue.text: Selection of food for a legislative assembly

explanation.surface: Choosing a menu for parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular choice of meals is one's eating regime; separately, several countries' parliaments, such as Japan's, bear this name.

clue.text: Peacekeepers restraining opponents? Feasible but thankless

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces
E and N are opposing partners at bridge
viable means feasible

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers holding back enemy forces have a workable but ungrateful job.
explanation.walkthrough: East and North (E, N) are opponents at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: A task nobody would envy is thankless, bringing no gratitude or reward.

clue.text: Just over 500? It's a bargain!

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a number just over 500 is 501: add one to it

explanation.surface: A price a little above 500 is a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Five hundred and one is D plus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation agreeing to a deal, sealing it.

clue.text: Well-bred people, quiet and not from the county

parts.note: gentle means soft, quiet

indicators.note: from means taking the first piece away from the county's name

parts.note: Norfolk is an English county
nor means and not

explanation.surface: Refined people, quiet and not local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and not from the county' looks like an outsider, but NOR (and not) is removed from NORFOLK, an English county, to leave FOLK.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the gentry, people of good family and breeding.
